app: User-interface text of RealMap, a desktop app that turns a real-world area (relief from elevation data, rivers, lakes and sea, towns, industrial sites, roads and railways from OpenStreetMap) into a custom map for the city-building / transport video game Transport Fever 3. The user picks the area on a map, the app fetches the real data, computes the game map (heights, water, towns with their sizes, industries, road links, a buildable railway line), shows the result on the map, then writes the files and its in-game mod builds everything in the game's Map Editor.

sections.lang: Name of the language in the language list.
sections.tabs: Tabs of the left panel: the three steps of the app (area and data, advanced options, export to the game) and the log.
sections.data: Tab 1 › Game map: size, format and scale of the game map, and the data sources (elevation, land cover). Its bottom button fetches the real data.
sections.data.source: Tab 1 › Sources: where the relief (elevation) comes from.
sections.advanced: Tab 2 › Advanced options: how the real data becomes the game map (relief, water depths and banks, towns, industries, roads, railway: its curve radius, gradient, distance to towns and how far it may leave the real line to suit the game's relief). Field labels sit two side by side in a narrow panel: keep them short. Its bottom button recomputes the result.
sections.export: Tab 3 › Export: map name, game folder, and the button that writes the files and builds the map in the game's Map Editor.
sections.step.data: Tab 1: list of the data downloads in progress (one line per source).
sections.step.export: Tab 3: list of the export steps done by the app.
sections.step.game: Tab 3: list of the steps the in-game mod runs in the Map Editor (shown after 'Game: ').
sections.status: Bottom bar of the panel: link next to an error message.
sections.log: Log tab: messages of the app, with a toggle for technical details.
sections.map: Map next to the panel: toolbar, hover tooltips (what is under the mouse), road and railway names, banner while picking the end of a new road or railway line.
sections.menu: Right-click menu on the map: add or remove a town or an industry, link two towns by road, draw a railway line, add an industry, delete a road or a railway line.
sections.sheet: Information card of a town or an industry clicked on the map (one fact per line).
sections.lists: Lists panel over the map: towns, industries, roads and railway lines of the result, with check boxes to keep or leave them out.
sections.legend: Map legend: colours and symbols of the result shown on the map.
sections.roads: Roads section of the Advanced options tab: whether the roads between towns are chosen automatically or were changed by hand, and the button (with a confirmation) that goes back to the automatic choice, forgetting the user's changes.
sections.size: Names of the game's map sizes (as in the game's new map dialog), and the size line '<size> (<format>) — <width> × <height> km'.
sections.cover: Land cover classes shown on the map (open land, forest, scrub, rock).
sections.origin: Information card of an industry: where the industry comes from.
sections.originShort: Lists panel: very short tag of where an industry comes from.
sections.place: Kind of place in OpenStreetMap (city, town, village).
sections.industry: Names of the game's industry types (use the game's official names).
sections.cargo: Names of the game's cargo types, in lists after 'commercial:' / 'industrial:' (use the game's official names, lower case).
sections.credits: Data credits at the bottom of the panel (keep the names and licences).
sections.mod: In-game window of the RealMap mod inside Transport Fever 3's Map Editor, and the report lines it sends back to the app.
sections.industry.nameOf: Name the app gives a generated industry, which becomes its name in the game: {industry} = the industry type (the game's name), {town} = the nearest town. Use the word order a native speaker would use for a place-named business (English: 'Lyon Saw Mill').
sections.progress: Status line under the progress bar while the app computes the game map: the current computation stage.
sections.net: Download status of an OpenStreetMap (Overpass) request, shown next to a data step or in an error: {server} is a server name.
sections.why: Reason shown on the card of a town or an industry (why it was moved or left out, or why an industry is there), after a label such as 'left out:' or 'origin:'. Lower case, no final full stop.
sections.msg: Messages of the Log tab and of the panel's status line: download details, warnings when a data source fails, the summary of the computed map, the export and in-game generation steps.
sections.updates: App updates, in a section of the Export tab and a badge in the header: installed version, check for a new version on GitHub, install it and restart the app, release notes, skip a version, check at startup. {version} is a version number like 1.1.0.
